questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Choosing James Cook University in Townsville, Australia, was influenced by its academic excellence, especially in marine biology and environmental science, and its unique location near the Great Barrier Reef. The university's supportive learning environment, modern facilities, and dedicated international student services were crucial factors. Additionally, the opportunity to immerse myself in Australian culture and participate in numerous field trips to study diverse ecosystems made it an ideal study destination

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I spent a considerable amount of time finding the information I needed upon arrival, especially regarding course selection and other academic details. However, once I arrived at James Cook University, the staff were very helpful in assisting me with everything I needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arriving at my study destination, the assistance I received made the transition remarkably easy. James Cook University offered a convenient pick-up service from the airport, taking me directly to my on-campus accommodation. This support was invaluable in helping me settle in quickly and comfortably, ensuring a smooth start to my exchange program

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were several accommodation options available on campus. I stayed at Burrelga Yumba (BY), where I had my own room and shared a communal bathrooms and kitchen. The facilities were very new and modern, making for a comfortable living experience, and it was only a 2-5 minute walk to my classes. However, with over 400 people living there, it wasn't the most social place unless you made an effort to engage with others. It was convenient for a semester, and the cleaning service every other week was a nice touch. While it wasn't the coziest environment, I found social opportunities elsewhere

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At Burralga Yumba, we shared a large communal kitchen among 400 people. This could be quite stressful, so I made sure to meal prep a few times a week. Burralga Yumba didn't offer meal plans, so we were responsible for our cooking. However, other accommodation options on campus did offer meal plans, though I didn't hear much positive feedback about them.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend living on campus if you're only going for a semester. I found Burralga Yumba (BY) to be okay, but for a better social experience, I'd suggest either Rotary or the Townhouses. In these accommodations, you share a kitchen with 8-10 people, making it easier to meet new people. It's also much easier to participate in social activities when you live on campus, as public transport in Townsville is not very reliable

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at my host institution was quite frustrating and time-consuming. I was nominated for the exchange program in the spring a year before I departed, but I didn't receive an official placement until half a year later. Once accepted, navigating the course registration on their website was incredibly confusing. They had a peculiar timetable layout which made it difficult to understand when courses overlapped. Overall, this part of the process was quite challenging, and there were moments where I almost gave up

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The help available initially was limited to email correspondence due to the time difference making it impractical to call them. It wasn't until I arrived and visited their office in person that I received more effective assistance. Before arriving, there were many issues I struggled to resolve remotely and was unsure how to navigate. Fortunately, they were very helpful once I was on campus, though I wish I had known more about their support beforehand.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registering for classes was incredibly challenging for me. I ended up changing my courses multiple times because it was difficult to ascertain the content and prerequisites required for each. There was even a course I enrolled in that I did not have the necessary background for, despite the description indicating no prerequisites were needed. This process was frustrating and required a lot of adjustments throughout the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice to future exchange students regarding registration at my host institution would be to carefully use their timetable website to check for course overlaps. It's crucial to thoroughly review the course descriptions to understand the expected prior experience or prerequisites. Additionally, I would recommend reaching out to academic advisors or student services early on for guidance and clarification, as the registration process can be confusing. Being proactive and seeking help as soon as possible upon arrival can save a lot of time and frustration later on.

questions.answer: As a second-year student during my exchange, I enrolled in courses that were typically designated as second and third-year level at James Cook University

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at my host institution differed from UCPH, especially regarding exams and course delivery. Exams were typically lecture-based without supplementary reading materials, which could be challenging with less effective lecturers. Some courses relied heavily on lectures with limited written resources, and there were also online lectures with physical attendance required mainly for fieldwork. This mix required adapting to different teaching methods compared to what I experienced at UCPH

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a wide variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students at my host institution. From cultural festivals and art exhibitions to sports tournaments and fitness classes, there was something for everyone's interests. Socially, there were clubs and societies catering to various hobbies and causes, providing opportunities to meet new people and engage in meaningful activities. Overall, the host institution offered a vibrant campus life with numerous options for students to participate and enrich their exchange experience.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore Australia's natural wonders like the Great Barrier Reef and national parks. Attend local cultural events and festivals to experience traditions firsthand. Engage in outdoor sports such as surfing and hiking. Take road trips to discover scenic routes and hidden gems.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Magnetic Island is an amazing place for diving, snorkeling and seeing koalas!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the local culture was manageable due to Australians' friendliness and openness. Engaging in local activities and university events helped me understand and appreciate the cultural nuances better, despite occasional differences like the younger age of university students starting their studies. Overall, it was a rewarding experience with an open mind and willingness to embrace new experiences.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Joining clubs and societies is a fantastic way to socialize with local students during your exchange.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One cultural difference I found particularly challenging was the younger age at which people start university in Australia. Many students begin their university studies at around 17 years old, which was quite different from what I was accustomed to. Adjusting to this age gap in social settings and classrooms initially posed a challenge for me. As a result, I naturally gravitated towards forming friendships with other Scandinavians and international students who were closer to my age and had a similar academic background. This helped me feel more comfortable and find a sense of camaraderie during my time on exchange.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: What I most appreciated about the culture in Australia was the warmth and helpfulness of the people. Australians are genuinely friendly and welcoming, always ready to lend a hand or strike up a conversation.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Explore the Underwater World: Don't miss out on diving opportunities! The Great Barrier Reef and nearby areas offer unparalleled experiences for divers of all levels. Whether it's snorkeling or deep-sea diving, take the chance to explore Australia's rich marine life and stunning coral reefs.

2. Plan Road Trips and Explore: Consider renting or sharing a car with friends who have one. Australia's vast landscapes and natural wonders are best experienced through road trips. You can visit national parks, remote beaches, and charming towns beyond the city. It's a great way to appreciate the country's diverse beauty.

3. Build a Network and Embrace the Community: Connect with local and international students. Join clubs, participate in campus events, and engage in social activities. Building friendships and connections not only enriches your exchange experience but also helps you feel more at home in a new environment

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything I haven't written already

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the opportunity to immerse myself in a completely different academic and cultural environment. I gained a broader perspective on my field of study through interactions with professors and students who offered unique insights and approaches. Living in a new country also allowed me to explore diverse landscapes, traditions, and perspectives, enriching my personal growth and understanding of the world. Overall, the exchange experience challenged me to adapt, learn independently, and embrace new challenges, which ultimately broadened my horizons and left me with lasting memories and friendship

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was adjusting to a different style of learning and a new academic system. Courses often required handwritten exams, which was a departure from my usual experience. Additionally, not knowing anyone initially meant I had to actively engage in social activities to make friends and integrate into the community.
